title: How detergents clean, your raw materials, and staying safe
course_title: Detergent and Cleaning Products Production: Liquid Soap, Hand Wash and Safe Cleaning

say: How detergents clean, your raw materials, and staying safe.
This is the video for module one of Detergent and Cleaning Products Production.
Every cleaning product depends on one kind of ingredient, a surfactant. That word is short for surface active agent. One end, the head, loves water.

panel.heading: The surfactant: two different ends
items: Tails wrap each drop of oil

say: The other end, the tail, loves oil and grease, and hates water.

panel.heading: The surfactant: two different ends
items: Tails wrap each drop of oil

say: When you wash a greasy pot, the tails push into the grease, and thousands of molecules surround each small drop of oil.

panel.heading: The surfactant: two different ends
items: Tails wrap each drop of oil

say: Now the grease has a coat that water can hold, so rinsing carries it away. That is why plain water cannot remove palm oil from a plate, but water with detergent can.

panel.heading: The surfactant: two different ends
items: Tails wrap each drop of oil

say: The keg liquid soap sold in Nigeria is almost always a synthetic detergent, not true soap. Multipurpose liquid soap is a good first product, because everyone buys it again and again.
Liquid hand wash comes second, once the first is right every time.
Do not manufacture bleach or disinfectants as a beginner. Germ-killing claims need proof and approval.
A detergent cleans by lifting dirt and grease. Never label it as a disinfectant.
Sulphonic acid is a thick, dark brown, oily liquid. As bought, it is a strong, corrosive acid. It only becomes a cleaning agent after it is neutralised with an alkali.
SLES, often sold as texapon, is gentler on skin and foams well. A label saying 70% means 100 g of paste holds about 70 g of real surfactant. Buy on known strength, not just price.
Caustic soda is a strong alkali used to neutralise the acid. Soda ash is milder, and fizzes when it meets acid.
STPP is a builder. It ties up the minerals in hard water so the surfactant works better.
Nitrosol, CMC and salt give the product body. Remember, more foam does not mean better cleaning.
Many local recipes use formalin as a preservative. Formaldehyde is classed as a human carcinogen, so avoid it. Use a detergent preservative at the dose on its data sheet.

Sulphonic acid and caustic soda can burn skin and damage eyes within seconds. So work with a routine. Splash goggles that seal, gloves over the wrists, long sleeves, an apron and closed shoes. Mix outdoors or with open windows, never in your kitchen.

say: Household bleach mixed with acids, like many toilet cleaners, vinegar or sulphonic acid, releases chlorine gas.

panel.heading: Bleach never meets acid or ammonia
items: Never add bleach to your soap
Customers use bleach on its own

say: Mixed with ammonia, found in some glass cleaners and urine, it releases chloramine gases. Both can damage the lungs and kill.

panel.heading: Bleach never meets acid or ammonia
items: Never add bleach to your soap
Customers use bleach on its own

say: So never add bleach to any product you make, or put it in a container that once held acid.

panel.heading: Bleach never meets acid or ammonia
items: Never add bleach to your soap

say: Tell customers clearly. Use bleach on its own, rinse, then use other cleaners.

say: Keep a large container of clean water within reach. A splash in the eye needs rinsing with running water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open. Then go to a hospital.

cards.d: Rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes, eyelid open. Then go to hospital.
Remove soaked clothing. Rinse with running water for at least 15 minutes. No vinegar.
Fumes: get to fresh air. Swallowed: do not cause vomiting; go to hospital with the container.

say: On skin, remove soaked clothing and rinse for at least 15 minutes. Do not use vinegar or soda on a burn. Water is the right first aid.

say: If someone breathes fumes, leave for fresh air at once. If a chemical is swallowed, do not make the person vomit. Rinse the mouth and go to hospital with the container. And never store chemicals in drink bottles.

say: So remember. Surfactants let water carry grease away. Start with multipurpose liquid soap. Buy labelled chemicals and avoid formalin.
Add caustic and acid to water, slowly. And never mix bleach with other cleaners.

items: Surfactants let water carry grease away
Bleach never mixes with other cleaners
